methods: setting up a recurrence for alpha^n+beta^n
statement: The roots of $x^{2}-6x+4=0$ are $\\alpha$ and $\\beta$. For each integer $n\\ge0$, define $S_{n}=\\alpha^{n}+\\beta^{n}$. Show that $S_{n}$ satisfies $S_{n+2}=6S_{n+1}-4S_{n}$, and hence find $S_{5}$.
solution:
We have $\\alpha+\\beta=6$ and $\\alpha\\beta=4$. Then $S_{n+2}=\\alpha^{n+2}+\\beta^{n+2}=(\\alpha+\\beta)(\\alpha^{n+1}+\\beta^{n+1})-\\alpha\\beta(\\alpha^{n}+\\beta^{n})=6S_{n+1}-4S_{n}$. The initial values are $S_{0}=2$ and $S_{1}=6$. Hence $S_{2}=6\\cdot6-4\\cdot2=28$, $S_{3}=6\\cdot28-4\\cdot6=144$, $S_{4}=6\\cdot144-4\\cdot28=752$, and $S_{5}=6\\cdot752-4\\cdot144=3936$. Thus $S_{5}=3936$.
